## Introduction

In this post, I use Python to explore relationships between flower measurements in the Iris dataset.

Data: [Iris dataset](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/datasets/plot_iris_dataset.html), accessed through scikit-learn.

The dataset contains measurements of sepal and petal dimensions for three iris species.

## Load the data

```{python}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

iris = load_iris(as_frame=True)
df = iris.frame

df.head()
```

The dataset contains four numerical flower measurements and a target variable representing species.

## Summarize the measurements

```{python}
df.describe()
```

The summary shows the distributions of sepal length, sepal width, petal length, and petal width.

## Calculate mean measurements by species

```{python}
df["species"] = df["target"].map(
    dict(enumerate(iris.target_names))
)

species_means = df.groupby("species")[
    ["sepal length (cm)", "petal length (cm)"]
].mean()

species_means
```

The species differ substantially in their average petal lengths. Setosa has much shorter petals than versicolor and virginica.

## Visualize petal length and width

```{python}
#| label: fig-iris-petals
#| fig-cap: "Petal length and petal width for the three Iris species."

for species in df["species"].unique():
    subset = df[df["species"] == species]
    plt.scatter(
        subset["petal length (cm)"],
        subset["petal width (cm)"],
        label=species
    )

plt.xlabel("Petal length (cm)")
plt.ylabel("Petal width (cm)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```

The figure shows a strong positive relationship between petal length and petal width. Setosa is clearly separated from the other two species, while versicolor and virginica overlap somewhat.

## Conclusion

This analysis shows that Iris species differ noticeably in their flower measurements. Petal length and width are particularly useful for distinguishing the species.
